title: Traumatized teens sue school, cops after Doritos bag triggers AI gun alert
gist: Four Black Baltimore County students sued Omnilert, Baltimore County Public Schools and police after Omnilert's AI gun-detection flagged a Doritos bag; staff canceled the alert within two minutes, but the untrained principal missed the cancellation and called police, who held the teens at gunpoint and handcuffed them. The suit seeks an injunction on Omnilert use; the OIG found no system bias but flagged broken alert controls and that over 99% of BCPS gun alerts were false positives.

insights.claim: In October 2025, Omnilert's AI gun detection system at a Baltimore County high school flagged a student holding a bag of Cool Ranch Doritos as a potential gunman; school safety staff reviewed footage and canceled the alert within two minutes.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: High-profile false positive is a reputational and liability risk for AI security vendors selling to schools.

insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: Real-world precision of AI weapon detection is very low; the product depends on human review to be usable.

insights.claim: The OIG found Kenwood High principal Kate Smith, apparently never trained on Omnilert, missed the alert cancellation and texted a school resource officer to deploy police 15 minutes later while noting the object was 'maybe not' a gun.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: Untrained recipients of AI alerts are the weak link; deployments without training create legal exposure.

insights.claim: At least six police cars responded, some officers with guns drawn, and the teens were forced to their knees, handcuffed and searched; officers allegedly had not reviewed the footage and none who knew of the cancellation intervened.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: Escalation from AI alerts to armed police response is the core tail risk driving litigation and reform demands.

insights.claim: The students, represented by the Lawyers' Committee for Civil Rights Under Law, allege unlawful search and detention and seek an injunction barring Baltimore County Public Schools from using Omnilert until staff and police are adequately trained.
